title: Maxwell's Ribbon
hook: Rebuild a qubit the way Maxwell rebuilt colour.
sub: You can't look at a qubit, just as Maxwell couldn't photograph colour in 1861. He used three filters, and physicists use three measurements. Pick any colour and see what a quantum run gave back for it.
you_control: Pick a colour for the Bloch-ball sitter, or click a pixel of Maxwell's ribbon, and have Maxwell photograph it through X, Y and Z filters
Slide the shots: 16, 128 or 1024 measurements, and watch the plates and the rebuilt portrait sharpen
Switch machines: perfect simulator, Fez and Brisbane noise models, the real ibm_fez chip (the studio swaps in a computer or IBM's chip in its fridge)
Turn the 3D colour/qubit ball in 'The data' section (or open it in place of the scene) and see every test colour drift
Measure a hidden arrow along Z, X and Y to rebuild a hidden colour behind a curtain (classical tomography toy)
See where your colour sits (Z, X and Y bars) in chapter 3, and load any of the 10 cached jobs from the run table or the 'Jobs and credits' list
qubits_note: ibm_fez hardware run: 448 values filled the chip's full capacity, 64 data + 92 address = all 156 qubits in one joint circuit (IBM job db1jcnuegvvc73bhn5ng). qpixl-v1 does not report a qubit count. topology.py computes it from the chip's coupling map with the engine's documented checkerboard rule, which reproduces the capacities measured on the live engine (Fez 448, Brisbane 360, Torino 378). The fake_fez/fake_brisbane rows use the 156/127-qubit layouts, but the emulator simulates each data-qubit group (at most 4 qubits) separately. The aer lattice size is not reported. The guide's ceil(log2 #values)+1 shorthand would give 10 for 448 values; README explains the difference.
honesty: Every rebuilt colour comes from a real cached qpixl-v1 job, labelled by where it ran (aer simulator, fake_fez/fake_brisbane noise models, one ibm_fez hardware run). The colour split and rebuild are classical; photography and the colour ball are labelled analogies; this is not three-basis tomography of one qubit and no advantage is claimed.
blockers: tessa-image-v1, the engine named in the brief, failed 5 of 5 jobs with engine_timeout (two at 64x64, two at 32x32, one at 16 shots after a 9-minute wait; IDs in PARAMS.md), so no Tessa output exists. The piece runs Tessa's pipeline by hand on qpixl-v1 (same iqpixl library), documented on the page and in README/PARAMS/CREDITS.
The 15-credit cap is fully used (15 ledgered: 10 completed qpixl jobs + 5 failed Tessa jobs), so a Tessa rerun can't fit if the engine comes back.

Lead / entry 07: entry 07's PARAMS.md gives '9 address + 1 data = 10' for its 448-value qpixl-v1 ibm_fez run, while this entry gives 156 (64 data + 92 address) for the same capacity, counted from the coupling map. Entry 11's README labels both rules; entry 07 should be reconciled or labelled (not edited here).
